checks.explanation: Trump won the 2024 election and was inaugurated in January 2025.

Malibu wildfire rebuilding did face significant permitting delays through 2025-2026, consistent with the prediction's premise, though a definitive multi-decade blockage preventing any rebuilding is too early to fully confirm.

Taxpayers, insurers, and homeowners have all continued to absorb rising catastrophe losses through cost-sharing mechanisms (state insurers of last resort, federal disaster aid), without a single party clearly bearing the predominant burden.

California did seek federal disaster assistance following the January 2025 LA wildfires, though a full-scale distinct 'bailout' beyond standard FEMA disaster relief was not clearly and separately confirmed.
No successful recall of Governor Newsom or Mayor Bass occurred following the January 2025 wildfires.

Some investor and developer interest in acquiring burned Palisades lots at discounts did emerge, though a clear pattern of buying at steep 80% discounts and holding for the long term without redevelopment was not comprehensively confirmed.

State-backed insurance programs (California FAIR Plan) did face mounting strain and reform pressure after the 2025 wildfires, with some regulatory changes advancing, though comprehensive federal or state legislative reform ending subsidies had not fully materialized by mid-2026.
Tesla did not acquire Uber; the two companies remained separate as Tesla pursued its own robotaxi service independently.

Robotics and robotaxi markets did see substantial growth through 2025-2026 (Waymo scaling, Tesla's robotaxi launch), consistent with significant expansion, though whether it constitutes the single largest robotics breakout ever is a subjective, hard-to-verify claim.

Waymo did emerge as the clear US robotaxi market leader by 2025-2026 with Tesla scaling its own service, broadly matching the prediction, though a broad wave of traditional auto OEM consolidation specifically attributable to this has not been clearly confirmed.

AI did trigger a significant surge of new startups and rapid, parallel product development through 2025-2026, widely described in venture circles as increasing competitive pressure and difficulty for early-stage investors to differentiate winners.

Discussions around Arctic shipping routes and US interest in Greenland intensified through 2025 (including Trump's stated interest in acquiring Greenland), though a fully commercially viable Northern Passage comparable in importance to the Panama Canal had not yet materialized by mid-2026.
The Magnificent Seven's weight in the S&P 500 did not fall below 30% by the end of 2025; it stood at roughly 34% as of December 2025.
US national debt surpassed $38 trillion in October 2025, confirming this prediction within calendar year 2025.

Actual deportations during 2025 fell well short of 750,000; ICE removals were reported around 442,000 for fiscal year 2025 and roughly 200,000 in the first several months of Trump's term, below the predicted threshold.
